sections.name: Chapter 13 · Healthy Living, Nutrition and Stress

items.q: Which activity increases the production of endorphins, the hormones secreted by the body that produce feelings of well-being?
items.ex: Physical activity stimulates the release of endorphins, which reduce pain and create a sense of well-being (the "runner's high").
w: Good relationships support well-being, but exercise is what's known to trigger endorphin release.
Enjoyable food can lift mood briefly, but the endorphin link taught here is exercise.
Sleep restores the body and mind; it isn't the activity linked to an endorphin boost.

alt.q: Endorphins, the body's "feel-good" hormones, are released most reliably during which activity?
alt.ex: Physical activity stimulates the release of endorphins, which reduce pain and create a sense of well-being (the "runner's high").
w: Being sedentary doesn't trigger endorphin release.
A big meal can cause drowsiness, not an endorphin boost.
Rest is restorative but isn't the endorphin trigger.

tf: Physical activity increases the body's production of endorphins.
Sleeping well is the main way to increase the body's production of endorphins.
Exercise, not sleep, is the activity linked to endorphin release.
ty: Endorphins are released when you engage in physical ________. (one word)
activity
exercise
Physical activity stimulates the release of endorphins, which reduce pain and create a sense of well-being (the "runner's high").

items.q: Which of the following is the major reason that smoking is a difficult habit to break?
items.ex: Nicotine is highly addictive. Stopping causes withdrawal symptoms, which makes quitting hard.
w: Most people lack the necessary willpower.
Willpower matters, but the main barrier is physical addiction to nicotine.
It is a good stress reducer.
Smoking feels calming only because it relieves nicotine withdrawal; it isn't a true stress reducer.
Enjoyment isn't the main reason; nicotine dependence is.

alt.q: Why do many smokers find it so hard to quit?
alt.ex: Nicotine is highly addictive. Stopping causes withdrawal symptoms, which makes quitting hard.
w: They don't know smoking is harmful.
Most smokers know the risks; addiction is the barrier.
Cost doesn't explain the difficulty; cigarettes are costly.
Any short-term focus is relief from withdrawal, not a real benefit.

tf: Smoking is hard to quit mainly because nicotine is addictive.
Smoking is hard to quit mainly because it is a good stress reducer.
Nicotine addiction, not stress relief, makes smoking hard to quit.
ty: Smoking is hard to quit because ________ is an addictive substance.
nicotine
Nicotine is highly addictive. Stopping causes withdrawal symptoms, which makes quitting hard.
items.hint: Which chemical in tobacco causes dependence?

items.q: Which of the following statements is true about processed foods?
items.a: Many processed food packages contain more than one serving.
items.ex: Read labels carefully: one package often holds several servings, so the calories, sugar and sodium listed are per serving, not per package.
w: Processed foods contain low amounts of added sugar.
Processed foods are often high in added sugar.
Processed foods tend to have low levels of sodium.
Processed foods are a major source of sodium in the American diet.
Trans fats are not present in processed foods.
Trans fats have been found in processed foods (partially hydrogenated oils).

alt.q: When reading the nutrition label on a packaged snack, what should you check first?
alt.a: How many servings the package contains
alt.ex: Read labels carefully: one package often holds several servings, so the calories, sugar and sodium listed are per serving, not per package.
w: Packaging color tells you nothing about nutrition.
"Natural" is loosely defined; servings per package affect every number on the label.
The brand doesn't change how to read the label.

tf: A single package of processed food often contains more than one serving.
Processed foods tend to be low in sodium.
Processed foods are usually high in sodium, and packages often contain more than one serving.
items.hint: Look at the "servings per container" line on a label.

items.q: Which of the following statements is 100% effective at preventing sexually transmitted diseases?
items.ex: Only abstinence is 100% effective. Condoms, screening and open communication reduce risk but don't eliminate it.
w: Discuss the risk factors with your potential partner.
Talking lowers risk but doesn't guarantee protection.
Get regular screenings because some diseases have no signs or symptoms.
Screening finds infections early; it doesn't prevent them.
Condoms greatly reduce risk but aren't 100% effective.
tf: Abstinence is the only 100% effective way to prevent sexually transmitted diseases.
Using condoms is 100% effective at preventing sexually transmitted diseases.
Condoms reduce risk a lot, but only abstinence is 100% effective.
ty: The only 100% effective way to prevent STDs is ________. (one word)
abstinence
abstaining
abstain
Only abstinence is 100% effective. Condoms, screening and open communication reduce risk but don't eliminate it.
items.hint: It means not having sexual contact at all.

items.q: A deficiency of which mineral can interfere with the blood's ability to carry oxygen?
items.ex: Iron is part of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in red blood cells. Too little iron causes iron-deficiency anemia.
w: Potassium is key for nerve and muscle function, including heart rhythm.
Magnesium supports muscles, nerves and bones, not oxygen transport.
Zinc supports immunity and wound healing.

alt.q: Iron-deficiency anemia reduces the blood's ability to do what?
alt.ex: Iron is part of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in red blood cells. Too little iron causes iron-deficiency anemia.
w: Clotting depends on platelets and clotting factors, not iron.
That's the job of white blood cells.
Iron deficiency doesn't mainly affect temperature control.

tf: Iron deficiency can reduce the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
Zinc deficiency is what reduces the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
Iron, part of hemoglobin, is needed to carry oxygen.
ty: Which mineral is part of hemoglobin and needed to carry oxygen?
iron
Iron is part of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in red blood cells. Too little iron causes iron-deficiency anemia.

items.q: Which term refers to the process of obtaining food necessary for health and growth?
items.ex: Nutrition is the process of taking in and using the food needed for health and growth.
w: Diet is the food a person usually eats.
Lifestyle is a person's overall way of living.
A habit is any repeated behavior.
tf: Nutrition is the process of obtaining the food necessary for health and growth.
Diet is the process of obtaining the food necessary for health and growth.
That's nutrition; diet is simply what a person usually eats.
ty: The process of obtaining the food needed for health and growth is called ________.
nutrition
Nutrition is the process of taking in and using the food needed for health and growth.

items.q: Which of the following is experienced by an individual who develops a physical tolerance to a drug?
items.a: They need to take increasingly higher doses of the drug.
items.ex: Tolerance means the body adapts so the same dose has less effect, and higher doses are needed to get the same result.
w: They can more easily stop using the drug.
Tolerance usually comes with dependence, making it harder to stop.
They receive increased benefits from the drug.
With tolerance, the same dose has less effect.
They need smaller doses of the drug.
tf: A person with drug tolerance needs higher doses to get the same effect.
A person with drug tolerance needs smaller doses to get the same effect.
Tolerance means the same dose works less, so higher doses are needed.
ty: With physical tolerance, a person needs ________ doses to get the same effect. (one word)
higher
larger
bigger
increasing
more
Tolerance means the body adapts so the same dose has less effect, and higher doses are needed to get the same result.
items.hint: The same dose works less and less.

items.q: Which of the following vitamins is necessary for the body to properly absorb calcium?
items.ex: Vitamin D helps the intestines absorb calcium, which keeps bones strong.
w: Vitamin C helps make collagen and heal wounds.
B12 is needed for red blood cells and nerves.
Vitamin A supports vision, skin and immunity.

alt.q: Which vitamin does the skin make in sunlight and helps the body absorb calcium?
alt.ex: Vitamin D helps the intestines absorb calcium, which keeps bones strong.
w: Vitamin K is needed for blood clotting.
Vitamin C supports collagen and wound healing.

tf: Vitamin D is needed for the body to absorb calcium.
Vitamin C is needed for the body to absorb calcium.
Vitamin D (not C) helps absorb calcium; vitamin C helps heal wounds.
ty: Which vitamin helps the body absorb calcium? (letter)
Vitamin D
D
vit D
Vitamin D helps the intestines absorb calcium, which keeps bones strong.

mt.q: Match each vitamin to its main job.
mt.ex: Vitamin D helps the intestines absorb calcium, which keeps bones strong.

items.q: Which of the following is believed to be the most serious effect of continual stress?
items.ex: Continual (chronic) stress weakens the immune system, leaving the body more open to illness. This is considered its most serious effect.
w: Stress can affect thinking, but the most serious effect is on immunity and overall health.
That's a real effect, but not the most serious one.
Lowered ability to perform in an emergency
Short-term stress actually helps you react in an emergency.
tf: Continual stress can weaken the immune system.
The most serious effect of continual stress is lowered work efficiency.
The most serious effect is a weakened immune system.
items.hint: Think about how stress affects your ability to fight off illness.

items.q: Which of the following body mass index (BMI) results is considered obese?
items.ex: BMI categories: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5–24.9 normal, 25–29.9 overweight, 30 or higher obese.
w: A BMI of 10 is far below normal (severely underweight).

alt.q: A patient's BMI is 31. Which category does this fall in?
alt.ex: BMI categories: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5–24.9 normal, 25–29.9 overweight, 30 or higher obese.

tf: A BMI of 30 or higher is considered obese.
A BMI of 20 is considered obese.
Obese starts at 30; 20 is in the normal range (18.5–24.9).
ty: Obesity starts at a BMI of ____.
BMI categories: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5–24.9 normal, 25–29.9 overweight, 30 or higher obese.

mt.q: Match each BMI to its category.
mt.ex: BMI categories: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5–24.9 normal, 25–29.9 overweight, 30 or higher obese.

items.q: Which nutrients are composed of units of sugars and provide the body with immediate energy?
items.ex: Carbohydrates are broken down into simple sugars (glucose), the body's quickest energy source.
w: Proteins are made of amino acids and build body structures.
Minerals are elements like iron and calcium; they don't supply energy.
Fats are made of fatty acids and give stored, longer-term energy.
tf: Carbohydrates are made of sugar units and provide immediate energy.
Proteins are made of sugar units and provide immediate energy.
Proteins are made of amino acids; carbohydrates are the sugars that give quick energy.
ty: Nutrients made of sugar units that give immediate energy are ________.
carbohydrates
carbs
carbohydrate
Carbohydrates are broken down into simple sugars (glucose), the body's quickest energy source.

mt.q: Match each nutrient to what it does.
pairs: Amino acids that build body structures
Stored energy; some come from nuts, seeds and olive oil
mt.ex: Carbohydrates are broken down into simple sugars (glucose), the body's quickest energy source.

items.q: Which number is subtracted from a healthy person's age to determine the target heart rate during exercise?
items.ex: Maximum heart rate ≈ 220 − age. The target range during moderate exercise is about 50–70% of that (higher for vigorous exercise).

alt.q: Using the standard formula, what is the estimated maximum heart rate of a 40-year-old?
alt.ex: Maximum heart rate ≈ 220 − age. The target range during moderate exercise is about 50–70% of that (higher for vigorous exercise).

tf: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 minus age.
Maximum heart rate is estimated as 250 minus age.
The formula is 220 − age.
ty: Estimated maximum heart rate = ____ minus age.
Maximum heart rate ≈ 220 − age. The target range during moderate exercise is about 50–70% of that (higher for vigorous exercise).

items.q: Which of the following are physical symptoms of burnout?
items.ex: Burnout shows up physically (fatigue, stomach problems, headaches), emotionally (negative feelings about work) and in behavior (mistakes, absences).
w: That's an emotional sign, not a physical one.
Making errors and taking longer to complete tasks
tf: Fatigue, gastrointestinal disorders and headaches are physical symptoms of burnout.
Increased absences from work are a physical symptom of burnout.
Absences are a behavioral sign; the physical symptoms are fatigue, GI problems and headaches.
items.hint: Look for the choice describing the body, not feelings or behavior.

items.q: Which of the following can cause difficulty sleeping if consumed late in the day?
items.ex: Chocolate, tea and cola all contain caffeine, a stimulant that can interfere with sleep.
w: Chocolate has caffeine, but so do the other choices.
Tea has caffeine, but so do the other choices.
Cola has caffeine, but so do the other choices.
tf: Chocolate, tea and cola all contain caffeine that can disturb sleep.
Only cola drinks contain enough caffeine to disturb sleep.
All three contain caffeine and can affect sleep.
ty: Chocolate, tea and cola can disturb sleep because they contain ________.
caffeine
Chocolate, tea and cola all contain caffeine, a stimulant that can interfere with sleep.
items.hint: What do all three have in common?

items.q: Which of the following are common food sources of proteins?
items.a: Meats, fish, eggs, legumes, and seeds
items.ex: Protein comes from animal foods (meat, fish, eggs, dairy) and plant foods like legumes (beans, lentils), nuts and seeds.
w: These mainly supply vitamins, minerals, fiber and carbohydrates.
tf: Meats, fish, eggs, legumes and seeds are good sources of protein.
Breads, cereals and pastas are the main sources of protein.
Breads and pastas are mainly carbohydrates.
ty: Beans and lentils are called ________, a plant source of protein.
legumes
legume
pulses
Protein comes from animal foods (meat, fish, eggs, dairy) and plant foods like legumes (beans, lentils), nuts and seeds.
items.hint: Think of foods that build muscle.

items.q: Which characteristic is best when setting a health improvement goal?
items.ex: Reasonable, realistic goals are achievable, which keeps motivation up and makes the change last.
w: Too challenging a goal often leads to giving up.
Overly ambitious goals are hard to keep.
The goal should be easy to accomplish.
Too easy a goal doesn't lead to real change.
tf: A health improvement goal should be reasonable.
A health improvement goal should be as ambitious as possible.
Realistic goals are easier to achieve and keep.
ty: A good health goal should be ________ (realistic). (one word)
reasonable
realistic
achievable
attainable
Reasonable, realistic goals are achievable, which keeps motivation up and makes the change last.
items.hint: Not too hard, not too easy.

items.q: What type of information is available using MyPlate, developed by the U.S. Department of Agriculture?
items.a: Recommended proportions of healthy food groups
items.ex: MyPlate shows how to balance a meal: about half fruits and vegetables, plus grains, protein and dairy.
w: How many calories to consume each day.
MyPlate shows proportions of food groups, not a daily calorie number.
The type of diet to follow
It's a general guide to balance, not a specific diet plan.
tf: MyPlate shows the recommended proportions of the healthy food groups.
MyPlate tells you exactly how many calories to eat each day.
MyPlate is about proportions of food groups, not calorie counts.
ty: MyPlate was developed by the U.S. Department of ________.
Agriculture
USDA
MyPlate shows how to balance a meal: about half fruits and vegetables, plus grains, protein and dairy.
items.hint: It's a picture of a plate divided into sections.

items.q: Which group of employees must be offered a hepatitis B vaccination by their employer?
items.a: Workers who are exposed to bodily fluids of patients
items.ex: OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard requires employers to offer the hepatitis B vaccine, free of charge, to workers with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials.
w: It's required based on exposure, not just workplace.
Workers who work with elderly patients
Age of patients isn't the criterion; exposure to blood or body fluids is.
Workers who are at high risk for illness
The rule is about occupational exposure to blood and body fluids.
tf: Employers must offer the hepatitis B vaccine to workers exposed to blood or body fluids.
Employers must offer the hepatitis B vaccine only to workers who care for elderly patients.
It's based on exposure to blood or body fluids (OSHA).
ty: Employers must offer workers exposed to body fluids the hepatitis ___ vaccine. (letter)
B
OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard requires employers to offer the hepatitis B vaccine, free of charge, to workers with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials.
items.hint: It's about exposure to blood and body fluids (OSHA).

items.q: What is the first step one needs to take to be successful when working to change a habit?
items.a: Be willing to change the habit.
items.ex: Change starts with being willing (motivated) to change. Planning, tracking, support and rewards come next.
w: Decide how you will track your progress.
Tracking helps, but it comes after deciding to change.
Set up a good support system.
Support helps, but willingness comes first.
Rewards help, but only once you've committed to change.
tf: The first step in changing a habit is being willing to change it.
The first step in changing a habit is planning rewards.
Willingness comes first; rewards and tracking come after.
items.hint: Nothing else works until this is in place.

items.q: Which sexually transmitted disease should all persons between 13 and 64 be tested for at least once as a part of a routine health exam or more often if they have had more than one sexual partner?
items.ex: The CDC recommends that everyone aged 13–64 be tested for HIV at least once, and those at higher risk at least yearly.
w: Routine chlamydia screening targets sexually active women under 25 and others at risk.
Syphilis screening is risk-based and in pregnancy.
Routine herpes testing isn't recommended for people without symptoms.
tf: The CDC recommends everyone aged 13–64 be tested for HIV at least once.
The CDC recommends everyone aged 13–64 be tested for genital herpes at least once.
The universal once-in-a-lifetime test is for HIV.
ty: Everyone aged 13–64 should be tested at least once for ____. (abbreviation)
HIV
human immunodeficiency virus
The CDC recommends that everyone aged 13–64 be tested for HIV at least once, and those at higher risk at least yearly.
items.hint: It's the virus that causes AIDS.

items.q: Which of the following is an example of an internal stressor?
items.ex: Internal stressors come from within the person, such as habits, attitudes and skills like poor time management. External stressors come from the environment or other people.
w: That comes from the environment: an external stressor.
That's another person: an external stressor.
That's imposed from outside: an external stressor.
tf: Poor time management skills are an internal stressor.
A demanding supervisor is an internal stressor.
A supervisor is external; internal stressors come from within, like poor time management.
items.hint: Internal = something about the person themselves.

items.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of bulimia?
items.a: Eating large quantities of food followed by self-induced vomiting
items.ex: Bulimia nervosa involves binge eating followed by purging, such as self-induced vomiting or laxative use.
w: Uncontrolled eating beyond the satisfaction of hunger
That describes binge eating without purging.
Eating many fewer calories than needed to maintain bodily functions
tf: Bulimia involves binge eating followed by purging, such as self-induced vomiting.
Bulimia involves eating far fewer calories than the body needs.
That's anorexia; bulimia is binge eating then purging.
ty: Bulimia is binge eating followed by ________ (vomiting or laxatives).
purging
purge
vomiting
Bulimia nervosa involves binge eating followed by purging, such as self-induced vomiting or laxative use.

items.q: Which of the following is a communication technique used to express feelings freely in a nonthreatening manner?
items.ex: Assertiveness means stating your feelings and needs honestly and respectfully, without being passive or aggressive.
w: That's organizing your time, not a communication style.
Mediation is a third party helping others settle a dispute.
tf: Assertiveness is expressing feelings freely in a nonthreatening manner.
Mediation is expressing your own feelings freely in a nonthreatening manner.
Mediation involves a third party; assertiveness is your own respectful expression.
ty: Expressing your feelings honestly but respectfully is called ________.
assertiveness
assertive
being assertive
Assertiveness means stating your feelings and needs honestly and respectfully, without being passive or aggressive.

items.q: Which statement accurately describes the relationship between personal health habits and major causes of death?
items.a: Unhealthy lifestyle habits increase the risk of chronic diseases and premature death.
items.ex: Many leading causes of death, like heart disease, some cancers and diabetes, are strongly influenced by habits such as smoking, diet, activity and stress.
w: Major causes of death are primarily determined by genetic factors.
Genes play a role, but lifestyle strongly influences heart disease, cancer and diabetes.
Leading a sedentary lifestyle has no consequences for health.
Inactivity raises the risk of heart disease, diabetes and obesity.
Personal health habits have no impact on major causes of death.
Habits like smoking, diet and exercise strongly affect leading causes of death.

sc.title: Reggie, nurse practitioner
sc.text: As a nurse practitioner in a primary care clinic, Reggie is passionate about promoting health and wellness among patients. Reggie leads by example and strives to maintain a healthy lifestyle. Reggie prioritizes regular exercise, healthy eating habits, getting good sleep, and keeping stress levels low. Reggie starts the day with a nutritious breakfast, packed with fruits, whole grains, and protein. Throughout the day, Reggie stays hydrated by drinking water and uses breaks to stretch and take walks around the neighborhood where the clinic is located. Reggie encourages patients to adopt a similar lifestyle, providing them with resources and support to make positive changes towards realistic healthy habits.

items.hint: Reggie's habits are meant to lower which risks?

items.q: Why is it significant for health care professionals like Reggie to maintain a healthy lifestyle?
items.a: To set a good example for patients and promote health and wellness
items.ex: Health care workers who model healthy habits are more credible when teaching patients, and they stay healthier themselves.
w: Appearance isn't the point of healthy habits.
To increase productivity and efficiency at work
That can be a side benefit, but the main reason is modeling health for patients.
To avoid disciplinary action from regulatory bodies
Personal habits like diet aren't regulated this way.

items.ex: Anorexia nervosa has the highest death rate of any mental illness, from starvation, heart problems and suicide.
w: Binge eating disorder carries health risks but is less often fatal.
Bulimia is dangerous, but anorexia has the highest death rate.
Purging is a behavior, not a separate eating disorder.
tf: Anorexia nervosa is the eating disorder most likely to be life-threatening.
Binge eating is the eating disorder most likely to be life-threatening.
Anorexia has the highest death rate.

nervosa

veggies

Fiber is indigestible plant material that aids digestion.
Carbohydrates are sugars used for energy.

amino acids
amino acid

items.q: Trans fats potentially harm the body by _______.
items.a: raising low-density lipoprotein (LDL) levels while decreasing high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels
items.ex: Trans fats raise LDL and lower HDL, increasing the risk of heart disease. Partially hydrogenated oils were the main source.
w: That isn't the main harm of trans fats.
Any fat is calorie-dense, but the specific harm is to cholesterol levels.
That isn't how trans fats harm the body.
tf: Trans fats raise LDL cholesterol and lower HDL cholesterol.
Trans fats lower LDL cholesterol and raise HDL cholesterol.
Trans fats do the opposite: raise LDL, lower HDL.

items.q: Your _____ determine(s) how you view situations and can be either positive or negative
items.ex: Attitude is your general way of viewing situations, positive or negative, and it shapes how you handle stress.
w: Opinions are views on specific topics.
Emotions are feelings that come and go; attitude is your overall outlook.
Stress is a reaction, not an outlook.
tf: Your attitude determines how you view situations and can be positive or negative.
Stress determines how you view situations and can be positive or negative.
That describes attitude.
ty: Your overall positive or negative outlook is your ________.
attitude
Attitude is your general way of viewing situations, positive or negative, and it shapes how you handle stress.

items.q: Which of the following statements is true about stress?
items.a: It is the body's physical reaction to perceived danger.
items.ex: Stress is the body's "fight-or-flight" reaction to perceived danger. Short-term stress can help; continual stress harms health.
w: Every effort should be made to avoid it.
Some stress is normal and even helpful; the goal is managing it.
Continual stress is not harmful if a person learns to adjust to it.
Continual stress harms health even if you get used to it.
Some stress (eustress) motivates and helps performance.
tf: Stress is the body's physical reaction to perceived danger.
All stress is harmful.
Some stress is helpful; stress is the body's reaction to perceived danger.

items.q: Which of the following is NOT a cholesterol-lowering food?
items.ex: Red meat like beef is high in saturated fat, which can raise cholesterol. Oatmeal, walnuts and salmon help lower it.
w: Oatmeal's soluble fiber lowers LDL cholesterol.
Walnuts contain healthy fats that help lower cholesterol.
tf: Beef is not a cholesterol-lowering food.
Oatmeal raises cholesterol.
Oatmeal's soluble fiber lowers cholesterol.
ty: Which red meat in the list is NOT cholesterol-lowering: oatmeal, beef, walnuts or salmon?
beef
Red meat like beef is high in saturated fat, which can raise cholesterol. Oatmeal, walnuts and salmon help lower it.
items.hint: Which one is high in saturated fat?

items.q: A common sign of burnout is having negative feelings about work.
items.ex: Negative feelings about work are an emotional sign of burnout.
items.ww: Negative feelings about work are a classic sign of burnout.

alt.q: Feeling negative about your work is unrelated to burnout.
alt.ex: It's one of the most common signs of burnout.

items.q: A major reason for individuals failing to quit smoking is ______
items.ex: Nicotine withdrawal (irritability, cravings, anxiety, trouble concentrating) is uncomfortable, and many people relapse to relieve it.
w: Many smokers want to quit; withdrawal is what defeats them.
Denial of the dangers of smoking
Many smokers want to quit; withdrawal is what defeats them.
tf: Discomfort from withdrawal symptoms is a major reason people fail to quit smoking.
Most people fail to quit smoking because they deny its dangers.
Withdrawal discomfort is the major barrier.
ty: Nicotine ________ symptoms make quitting smoking uncomfortable.
withdrawal
Nicotine withdrawal (irritability, cravings, anxiety, trouble concentrating) is uncomfortable, and many people relapse to relieve it.

items.q: The percentage of American teenagers who were reported to be obese in 2020 was about
items.ex: CDC data from 2017 to March 2020 show about 22% of U.S. adolescents (12–19 years old) had obesity.
tf: About 22% of American teenagers had obesity around 2020.
About 5% of American teenagers had obesity around 2020.
It was about 22%.

items.q: The BMI for normal weight is
items.ex: A normal BMI is 18.5 to 24.9. 25–29.9 is overweight and 30+ is obese.
tf: A normal BMI is below 25 (18.5–24.9).
A normal BMI is anything below 29.
Normal stops at 24.9.
ty: A normal BMI is 18.5 up to ____.
A normal BMI is 18.5 to 24.9. 25–29.9 is overweight and 30+ is obese.

items.q: Physical activity can lower the risk of back pain.
items.ex: Exercise strengthens the core and back muscles and keeps the spine flexible, lowering back pain risk.
items.ww: Regular exercise reduces back pain risk.

alt.q: Regular exercise increases the risk of back pain.
alt.ex: Exercise strengthens the back and core muscles.

items.q: Most stress is caused by conditions out of our control.
items.ex: Much stress comes from how we perceive and respond to situations (attitude, habits, time management), which we can control.
items.ww: Much stress comes from our own reactions and habits, which we can manage.

items.q: The vitamin that promotes the healing of wounds is _____
items.ex: Vitamin C is needed to make collagen, the protein that rebuilds skin and tissue during wound healing.
w: Vitamin A supports vision, skin and immunity.
B vitamins help with energy and nerves.
tf: Vitamin C promotes wound healing.
Vitamin D promotes wound healing.
Vitamin C (collagen) heals wounds; D is for calcium.
ty: Which vitamin helps make collagen for wound healing? (letter)
Vitamin C
C
vit C
Vitamin C is needed to make collagen, the protein that rebuilds skin and tissue during wound healing.

mt.q: Match each vitamin to its main job.
mt.ex: Vitamin C is needed to make collagen, the protein that rebuilds skin and tissue during wound healing.

items.q: The consequences for a health professional who is caught using painkillers that were intended for a patient are usually no more serious than a reprimand from a supervisor.
items.ex: Diverting a patient's drugs is a serious crime and ethics violation. It can mean losing your license, being fired and being prosecuted.
items.ww: Consequences include losing the license, termination and criminal charges.

items.q: It is estimated that _____of Americans are overweight or have obesity.
items.ex: About 7 in 10 U.S. adults are overweight or have obesity (CDC data show roughly 71–74%).
w: That's close to the obesity rate alone, not overweight plus obesity.
tf: About 71% of Americans are overweight or have obesity.
About 41% of Americans are overweight or have obesity.
About 41% is close to the obesity rate alone; overweight plus obesity is about 71%.

items.q: When working to develop new habits, it is helpful to reward yourself when you achieve your goals.
items.ex: Rewards reinforce new behavior and keep motivation up.

items.q: Heart disease, diabetes, and osteoporosis can be prevented by ______
items.ex: Regular exercise strengthens the heart, helps control blood sugar and weight, and builds bone density.
w: Posture helps the back but doesn't prevent these diseases.
Sleep supports health, but exercise is the key preventive habit here.
Avoiding all stress isn't possible or the answer.
tf: Regular exercise helps prevent heart disease, diabetes and osteoporosis.
Good posture prevents heart disease, diabetes and osteoporosis.
Exercise is the preventive habit.
ty: Heart disease, diabetes and osteoporosis can be prevented by physical ________.
exercise
activity
Regular exercise strengthens the heart, helps control blood sugar and weight, and builds bone density.

items.q: Which of the following is NOT effective in lowering blood pressure?
items.ex: Exercise, less salt and stress reduction (like meditation) all lower blood pressure. Simply going to bed early isn't a recognized treatment.
w: Meditation and relaxation can lower blood pressure.
tf: Reducing salt intake helps lower blood pressure.
Reducing salt intake raises blood pressure.
Less salt lowers blood pressure.
items.hint: Three are standard advice for hypertension.

items.q: Children who are overweight tend to have problems maintaining a healthy weight when they are adults.
items.ex: Childhood obesity often continues into adulthood.
items.ww: Overweight children often stay overweight as adults.

items.q: An effective time management plan can eliminate all stress and enable an individual to function efficiently.
items.ex: Time management reduces stress but can't eliminate it all; some stress is a normal part of life.

items.q: One recommendation of the Mediterranean diet is to include at least ______ serving(s) of fish or shellfish in the diet each week.
items.ex: The Mediterranean diet emphasizes vegetables, fruits, whole grains, olive oil and at least two servings of fish or seafood a week.
w: The recommendation is at least two.
The recommendation is at least two.
The recommendation is at least two.
tf: The Mediterranean diet recommends at least two servings of fish a week.
The Mediterranean diet recommends at least four servings of fish a week.
It's at least two.
ty: Mediterranean diet: at least ____ servings of fish per week.
two
The Mediterranean diet emphasizes vegetables, fruits, whole grains, olive oil and at least two servings of fish or seafood a week.

items.q: When making lifestyle changes to improve your health, it is recommended that you start by making as many changes as possible to start experiencing the benefits.
items.ex: Start with one or two small, manageable changes; too many at once leads to giving up.
items.ww: Making many changes at once usually backfires.

items.q: ______ is produced by the skin when it is exposed to the sun.
items.ex: Sunlight (UVB) on the skin starts the body's production of vitamin D.
w: The body makes vitamin A from beta-carotene in food, not from sunlight.
Vitamin E comes from foods like nuts and oils.
Vitamin K comes from leafy greens and gut bacteria.
tf: The skin produces vitamin D when exposed to sunlight.
The skin produces vitamin K when exposed to sunlight.
Sunlight makes vitamin D.
ty: The skin makes vitamin ___ in sunlight. (letter)
D
Vitamin D
Sunlight (UVB) on the skin starts the body's production of vitamin D.

mt.q: Match each vitamin to its main job.
mt.ex: Sunlight (UVB) on the skin starts the body's production of vitamin D.

items.q: Eating adequate amounts of _____ helps maintain a healthy bowel.
items.ex: Fiber adds bulk and keeps stool moving, preventing constipation and supporting bowel health.
w: Protein builds tissue; it doesn't add bulk to stool.
Sodium affects fluid balance, not bowel health.
Fiber is a type of carbohydrate, but fiber specifically keeps the bowel healthy.
tf: Fiber helps maintain a healthy bowel.
Sodium helps maintain a healthy bowel.
Fiber, not sodium, supports bowel health.
ty: Eating enough ________ prevents constipation.
fiber
fibre
Fiber adds bulk and keeps stool moving, preventing constipation and supporting bowel health.

mt.q: Match each nutrient to what it does.
pairs: Amino acids that build body structures
Stored energy; some come from nuts, seeds and olive oil
mt.ex: Fiber adds bulk and keeps stool moving, preventing constipation and supporting bowel health.

items.q: If a food label lists partially hydrogenated oil as an ingredient, this means the product contains _____
items.ex: Partial hydrogenation creates trans fats. The FDA has since removed them from the "generally safe" list, so they're rare now, but the label clue still applies.
w: Fish oil is an omega-3 source, not hydrogenated.
All fats contain fatty acids; the key point is trans fat.
tf: Partially hydrogenated oil means the product contains trans fats.
Partially hydrogenated oil means the product contains fish oil.
Partially hydrogenated = trans fat.
ty: Partially hydrogenated oil contains ________ fats.
trans
trans fat
trans fats
Partial hydrogenation creates trans fats. The FDA has since removed them from the "generally safe" list, so they're rare now, but the label clue still applies.
items.hint: The fat that raises LDL and lowers HDL.

items.q: Calories are associated with foods that cause weight gain.
items.ex: Calories are commonly associated with foods that cause weight gain, but a calorie is simply a unit of energy found in all foods. Weight gain comes from taking in more calories than you burn.
items.ww: Calories are commonly associated with weight gain.

alt.q: Calories are found only in foods that cause weight gain.
alt.ex: All foods have calories; weight gain comes from taking in more than you burn.

items.q: Which of the following foods would be best for providing quick energy after a game of tennis?
items.ex: A banana's carbohydrates are quickly turned into glucose for fast energy, and it also replaces potassium.
w: Eggs are mostly protein and fat, which digest slowly.
Nuts are mostly fat and protein, which give slower energy.
Chicken is protein, not a quick energy source.
tf: A banana provides quick energy because of its carbohydrates.
A piece of chicken provides the quickest energy after exercise.
Carbohydrates (banana) give quick energy; protein is slower.

items.q: The term “organic,” when applied to food crops, means they are
items.a: Grown without the use of chemical insecticides
items.ex: Organic crops are grown without synthetic pesticides (insecticides) and synthetic fertilizers; natural fertilizers like compost are allowed.
w: Climate has nothing to do with organic labeling.
Organic crops are weeded, often by hand or machine.
Grown without any type of fertilizer
Organic farming uses natural fertilizers like compost and manure.
tf: Organic crops are grown without synthetic chemical pesticides.
Organic crops are grown without any fertilizer at all.
Natural fertilizers like compost are allowed.
items.hint: What chemicals do organic farmers avoid?

items.q: Decreasing physical exercise results in the body needing fewer calories to function.
items.ex: Less activity burns fewer calories, so the same intake can lead to weight gain.

items.q: It is believed that ______ takes place during the last few hours of sleep.
items.ex: Deep sleep early in the night is linked to physical repair. The last few hours, with more REM sleep, are linked to mental recuperation.
w: The deepest, most restful sleep happens earlier in the night.
Physical repair happens mainly in deep sleep earlier in the night.
That isn't the term used for this stage.
tf: Mental recuperation is believed to take place during the last few hours of sleep.
Physical repair is believed to take place mainly during the last few hours of sleep.
Physical repair is early (deep sleep); mental recuperation is late (REM).

items.q: The typical American diet tends to be high in calories and salt.
items.ex: Americans eat more calories and sodium than recommended, much of it from processed foods.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT put health care professionals at risk for burnout?
items.a: Easy access to addictive drugs, such as painkillers
items.ex: Easy access to drugs is a risk for substance misuse, not a cause of burnout. Emotional strain, lack of support and hard conditions cause burnout.
w: Emotional involvement with patients who are dying
That emotional strain is a burnout risk.
Lack of support raises burnout risk.
tf: Lack of emotional support puts health care workers at risk for burnout.
Working under difficult conditions protects against burnout.
Difficult conditions raise burnout risk.
items.hint: Which choice is a risk for something else (substance misuse)?

items.q: The BMI for a female who is 5’2” tall and weights 138 pounds is
items.ex: BMI = 703 × weight (lb) ÷ height (in)². 5′2″ = 62 in; 62² = 3,844; 703 × 138 = 97,014; 97,014 ÷ 3,844 ≈ 25.2, which is in the overweight range.
tf: A woman who is 5′2″ and 138 lb has a BMI of about 25.2 (overweight).
A woman who is 5′2″ and 138 lb has a BMI of about 21.9 (normal).
ty: BMI for 5′2″ (62 in) and 138 lb = 703 × 138 ÷ 62² = ____ (one decimal)
BMI = 703 × weight (lb) ÷ height (in)². 5′2″ = 62 in; 62² = 3,844; 703 × 138 = 97,014; 97,014 ÷ 3,844 ≈ 25.2, which is in the overweight range.

items.q: The goal of meditation is to quiet the mind by clearing it of thoughts.
items.ex: Meditation quiets the mind by focusing attention (on breath, a word or an image) and letting distracting thoughts go.
items.ww: Quieting the mind is the goal.

items.q: Many serious health conditions, such as heart disease, are strongly influenced by personal health habits.
items.ex: Smoking, diet, exercise and stress strongly influence heart disease and other chronic conditions.

items.q: Obesity is one of the leading causes of preventable deaths in the United States.
items.ex: Obesity, along with tobacco use, is among the top preventable causes of death in the U.S.
items.ww: It is one of the leading preventable causes.

sections.name: Chapter 14 · Human Needs, Culture and Diversity

items.q: Which of the following is the best description of Maslow's hierarchy of human needs?
items.a: Categories of needs ranked in order of importance
items.ex: Maslow ranked human needs in levels; lower, more basic needs generally must be met before higher ones. Maslow's levels, bottom to top: physiological (food, water, shelter) → safety and security → love and belonging (affection) → self-esteem → self-actualization (reaching full potential).
w: The hierarchy is about the needs themselves, not reactions to them.
It covers all human needs, not only health care.
It ranks needs; it doesn't describe behaviors.
tf: Maslow's hierarchy ranks categories of needs in order of importance.
Maslow's hierarchy describes behaviors people use in response to needs.
It's a ranking of needs, not behaviors.

items.q: Which of the following is true of someone who has high self-esteem?
items.ex: Self-esteem means valuing and respecting yourself. It's the fourth level of Maslow's hierarchy.
w: Self-esteem isn't the same as personality.
tf: High self-esteem means having self-respect.
High self-esteem means having above-average intelligence.
Self-esteem is self-respect.
ty: Self-esteem means having self-________. (one word)
respect
worth
value
Self-esteem means valuing and respecting yourself. It's the fourth level of Maslow's hierarchy.

items.q: Which distance is usually considered most comfortable when speaking with an acquaintance in the United States?
items.ex: Most Americans keep about 2 feet or more of personal space in conversation; closer distances are reserved for intimate relationships. Comfortable distances vary by culture.
w: That's intimate distance, for very close relationships.
That's the edge of intimate space; most Americans prefer a little more with acquaintances.
That's still very close for an acquaintance.
tf: Most Americans are comfortable standing about 2 feet from an acquaintance.
Most Americans are comfortable standing about 6 inches from an acquaintance.
6 inches is intimate distance.
items.hint: An arm's length or a bit less.

items.q: Natasha has been hospitalized following surgery. When their nurse gives them information about available pain medication and how to call for a nurse, which need is the nurse helping Natasha meet?
items.ex: Knowing pain will be managed and help is a call away makes a patient feel safe and secure. Maslow's levels, bottom to top: physiological (food, water, shelter) → safety and security → love and belonging (affection) → self-esteem → self-actualization (reaching full potential).
w: That's about belonging and caring relationships.
That's about feeling respected and valued.
That's about reaching one's full potential.
tf: Explaining how to call the nurse helps a patient meet safety and security needs.
Explaining how to call the nurse helps a patient meet self-actualization needs.
It's about feeling safe.
ty: Showing a patient how to call for help meets their ________ and security needs.
safety

Knowing pain will be managed and help is a call away makes a patient feel safe and secure. Maslow's levels, bottom to top: physiological (food, water, shelter) → safety and security → love and belonging (affection) → self-esteem → self-actualization (reaching full potential).

mt.q: Match each level of Maslow's hierarchy to what it means.
mt.ex: Knowing pain will be managed and help is a call away makes a patient feel safe and secure. Maslow's levels, bottom to top: physiological (food, water, shelter) → safety and security → love and belonging (affection) → self-esteem → self-actualization (reaching full potential).

items.q: Which of the following can health care professionals do to help patients deal with loss?
items.ex: Helping with loss means recognizing what it means to the patient, understanding their reaction, and being willing to talk about it.
w: Realize the significance of the loss to the patient.
True, but the other choices also help.
Understand the patient's reaction to their loss.
True, but the other choices also help.
Be willing to talk with patients about their loss.
True, but the other choices also help.

items.q: Which of the following describes "humors" that some members of Hispanic cultures believe must be balanced to maintain good health?
items.ex: The humoral (hot-cold) theory holds that health depends on balancing the body's humors, which are body fluids.
w: Humors are physical body fluids, not spirits.
That's closer to the Chinese idea of qi, yin and yang.
tf: In humoral theory, the humors are body fluids.
In humoral theory, the humors are spirits.
Humors are body fluids.
ty: In humoral theory, humors are body ________.
fluids
fluid
The humoral (hot-cold) theory holds that health depends on balancing the body's humors, which are body fluids.

items.q: Which of the following is true about implicit bias?
items.a: An individual is not aware they are biased.
items.ex: Implicit bias is unconscious: attitudes we hold without knowing it that can affect how we treat people.
w: The biased opinion is based on fact.
Most people do not experience it.
Almost everyone has some implicit bias.
It can affect how patients are treated.
tf: Implicit bias is unconscious; the person isn't aware of it.
Most people never experience implicit bias.
Nearly everyone has some implicit bias.
ty: Unconscious attitudes that affect how we treat others are called ________ bias.
implicit
unconscious
Implicit bias is unconscious: attitudes we hold without knowing it that can affect how we treat people.

items.q: Which ethnic group has traditionally based its health care on the concept of the opposing energy forces of yin and yang?
items.ex: Traditional Chinese medicine sees health as a balance of yin and yang and the flow of qi (energy).
w: Traditional Native American healing focuses on harmony with nature and spirit.
Some Hispanic traditions use the hot-cold humoral theory.
Yin and yang come from Chinese philosophy.
tf: Yin and yang are part of traditional Chinese health beliefs.
Yin and yang are part of traditional Hispanic health beliefs.
Yin and yang come from Chinese tradition.
ty: Yin and yang are part of traditional ________ medicine.
Chinese
Traditional Chinese medicine sees health as a balance of yin and yang and the flow of qi (energy).

items.q: Which of the following factors is achieved by communicating to patients that they are worth your time?
items.ex: Showing patients they matter supports their self-esteem. Maslow's levels, bottom to top: physiological (food, water, shelter) → safety and security → love and belonging (affection) → self-esteem → self-actualization (reaching full potential).
w: Those are food, water and shelter.
tf: Telling patients they're worth your time supports their self-esteem.
Telling patients they're worth your time meets their physiological needs.
It supports self-esteem.

items.q: Which of the following must be integrated and in balance for good health, according to some cultures?
items.ex: Many cultures (for example many Native American traditions) believe health requires harmony of mind, body and spirit.
w: The usual trio is mind, body and spirit.
The usual trio is mind, body and spirit.
The usual trio is mind, body and spirit.
tf: Some cultures believe mind, body and spirit must be in balance for good health.
Some cultures believe only the body matters for good health.
The belief is about mind, body and spirit.
ty: Some cultures believe health requires balance of mind, body and ________.
spirit
soul
Many cultures (for example many Native American traditions) believe health requires harmony of mind, body and spirit.

items.q: Which of the following actions is an example of prejudice?
items.a: Jose believes that older adults who come to the clinic are a drain on the health care system.
items.ex: Prejudice is a negative opinion about a whole group formed without knowing the individuals, like Jose's view of older adults.
w: Mason is interested in the cultures of India.
Interest in other cultures isn't prejudice.
Dan is learning Spanish so he can better communicate with patients who speak Spanish.
Jannah believes that abortion is wrong under most circumstances and tells her patients about her belief.
That's sharing a personal belief (unprofessional), but it isn't a prejudgment of a group of people.
tf: Believing all older patients are a drain on the system is prejudice.
Learning Spanish to help patients is prejudice.
Learning a patient's language is cultural sensitivity.
ty: A negative prejudgment about a group of people is called ________.
prejudice
Prejudice is a negative opinion about a whole group formed without knowing the individuals, like Jose's view of older adults.

items.q: Which term means the values, shared beliefs, and customs of a group of people?
items.ex: Culture is the values, shared beliefs, customs and behaviors of a group. It's learned, not inherited.
w: Race refers to physical and ancestral traits, not shared beliefs.
tf: Culture is the values, shared beliefs and customs of a group.
Race is the values, shared beliefs and customs of a group.
That's culture.
ty: The shared values, beliefs and customs of a group are its ________.
culture
Culture is the values, shared beliefs, customs and behaviors of a group. It's learned, not inherited.

items.q: Which is the best way for health care professionals to approach working with patients from a wide variety of backgrounds?
items.a: Use the interactions to enrich their own lives.
items.ex: Seeing diversity as an opportunity to learn and grow leads to more respectful, culturally sensitive care.
w: Just treat all patients the same.
Equal respect matters, but care should fit each patient's culture and needs.
Ignoring differences can lead to misunderstandings and poor care.
Refer to it as a difficult challenge.
Seeing diversity as a burden doesn't help patients.
items.hint: Which choice treats diversity as a positive?

items.q: Which of the following is an example of a patient experiencing loss?
items.ex: Loss includes death of a loved one, loss of a body part or function, and loss of independence or home.
w: Helen's spouse of 62 years died recently.
True, but the others are losses too.
Jackie had a mastectomy last month.
True: loss of a body part is a loss.
Nathan has just entered a skilled nursing facility.
True: loss of home and independence is a loss.

items.q: Which of the following is the reason Tai Chi is becoming popular in the United States?
items.ex: Tai Chi, a slow, flowing Chinese exercise, improves balance and flexibility and helps prevent falls, especially in older adults.
w: That isn't its main recognized benefit.
tf: Tai Chi improves balance and flexibility.
Tai Chi can replace prescription medications.
It improves balance; it doesn't replace medicine.

items.q: Which of the following is appropriate for a health care professional to ask a patient who is from a culture different from the dominant culture of the United States?
items.a: "Who in your family is responsible for making health decisions?"
items.ex: In many cultures, family members or elders make health decisions. A neutral, open question respects that.
w: "Why do you let your spouse make decisions about your health?"
"How do you expect to get better if you let others make decisions for you?"
"Why are you unable to make decisions for yourself?"
items.hint: Which question is neutral, not judgmental?

items.q: Which term means the transferring of feelings about one person to another person?
items.ex: Displacement redirects feelings from the real source to a safer target, like being angry at a nurse instead of at the illness.
w: Making up for a weakness or loss with another behavior.
Expressing feelings through behavior instead of words.
Faking or exaggerating illness for a gain.
tf: Displacement is transferring feelings about one person onto another.
Compensation is transferring feelings about one person onto another.
That's displacement.
ty: Transferring feelings about one person onto another is called ________.
displacement
Displacement redirects feelings from the real source to a safer target, like being angry at a nurse instead of at the illness.

mt.q: Match each defense mechanism to what it means.
pairs: Blaming others for your own faults
Moving feelings onto a safer target
Making up for a loss with another behavior
mt.ex: Displacement redirects feelings from the real source to a safer target, like being angry at a nurse instead of at the illness.

items.q: Which statement best describes how cultures relate to each other?
items.a: Behaviors considered positive in one culture may be negative in another.
items.ex: Eye contact, touch and personal space, for example, are polite in some cultures and rude in others.
w: Most cultures are quite similar in their values.
Guidelines for behavior are similar in most cultures.
Guidelines for behavior vary a lot.
It is unreasonable to expect people from different cultures to understand each other.
Understanding is possible with learning and respect.
tf: A behavior seen as positive in one culture can be negative in another.
Behavior guidelines are similar in most cultures.
They vary widely.

items.q: Which of the following medical assistants is applying the philosophy of individual worth?
items.a: Samantha treats patients who are gay with the same respect she shows other patients.
items.ex: The philosophy of individual worth means every person deserves respect, whatever their background, choices or circumstances.
w: Jason believes it is their duty to tell people who use drugs and come to the clinic that they would be better off if they stopped using drugs.
That's lecturing patients, not respecting their worth.
Taisha believes that patients who do not speak English should try to understand what they are saying.
That puts the burden on the patient.
Sandhya has trouble showing kindness to patients who do not follow their physician's advice.
items.hint: Which person shows respect to everyone?

items.q: Which of the following is the best way for the health care professional to determine a patient's health care beliefs?
items.ex: Each person is an individual. Observing and asking respectful questions is the only reliable way to learn their beliefs.
w: Base your knowledge on the patient's ethnicity.
Check the patient's chart for information.
Draw conclusions from the patient's appearance.

items.q: What is meant by the term dominant culture?
items.a: The generally accepted foundational beliefs and ideal behavior of a society
items.ex: Dominant culture is the set of beliefs and behaviors most people in a society accept as standard. In the U.S., an example is belief in democratic government.
w: The behaviors dictated by the laws of a country
Laws are part of it, but dominant culture is broader.
The culture of the people in power
It's about the majority's accepted beliefs, not just those in power.
The ideas of the people who have financial control
tf: Dominant culture is the generally accepted beliefs and ideal behavior of a society.
Dominant culture is the ideas of the people with financial control.
It's the generally accepted beliefs of a society.
ty: The foundational beliefs most people in a society share make up its ________ culture.
dominant
Dominant culture is the set of beliefs and behaviors most people in a society accept as standard. In the U.S., an example is belief in democratic government.

items.q: What do Christian Scientists believe that, to a great degree, recovery from illness is controlled by?
items.a: The faith and prayer of the individual
items.ex: Christian Science teaches that healing comes mainly through faith and prayer; members often decline medical treatment.
w: Christian Scientists traditionally rely on prayer rather than medicine.
That isn't the Christian Science belief.
tf: Christian Scientists believe recovery is largely controlled by faith and prayer.
Christian Scientists believe recovery is largely controlled by medical treatment.
They rely on faith and prayer.
ty: Christian Scientists rely mainly on faith and ________ for healing.
prayer
Christian Science teaches that healing comes mainly through faith and prayer; members often decline medical treatment.

items.q: What is the purpose of a defense mechanism?
items.a: Deal with conflict, problems, and threats to self-esteem.
items.ex: Defense mechanisms are mostly unconscious psychological strategies for coping with anxiety, conflict and threats to self-esteem.

items.q: Which statement illustrates a situation where a health care worker can leave a patient's protected health information on an answering machine?
