items.ex: Under HIPAA, protected health information can be left on a machine only with the patient's (written) permission; otherwise leave just your name and a callback number.
w: When the patient's results are for routine tests
Routine or not, results are protected health information.
When the health care worker is in a hurry
Being busy never justifies a privacy breach.
When the patient's spouse requests the information
A spouse needs the patient's authorization.
tf: PHI can be left on an answering machine only with the patient's written permission.
PHI can be left on an answering machine for routine test results.
Permission is needed even for routine results.

items.q: Mrs. Anderson is 89 and her daughter, Katherine, usually accompanies her to her doctor's appointments. Which is the correct way for the medical assistant to greet them?
items.ex: Address the patient directly and respectfully, by title and last name unless she asks otherwise.
w: "How is your mother doing today, Katherine?"
That talks about the patient as if she weren't there.
The patient should be greeted first.

items.q: Which of the following actions is required for active listening?
items.ex: Active listening means concentrating, paying full attention, and observing nonverbal cues.
w: Needed, but so are the others.
Needed, but so are the others.
Needed, but so are the others.

items.q: Which of the following is an example of an open-ended question?
items.ex: Open-ended questions can't be answered with yes or no and invite the patient to explain.
w: "Did you break your arm when you fell off your bike?"
That can be answered yes or no.
"Is this the first time you have broken a bone?"
"Does it hurt when I touch your arm here?"
tf: "How did you break your arm?" is an open-ended question.
"Does it hurt here?" is an open-ended question.
That's closed: yes or no.
ty: A question that can't be answered with yes or no is ________-ended.
open
Open-ended questions can't be answered with yes or no and invite the patient to explain.

mt.q: Match each type of question to an example.
pairs: "Can you tell me more about that?"
mt.ex: Open-ended questions can't be answered with yes or no and invite the patient to explain.

items.hint: It can't be answered yes or no.

items.q: Which of the following is the overall goal of therapeutic communication?
items.a: To meet the needs of the patient
items.ex: Therapeutic communication is purposeful, patient-centered communication aimed at meeting the patient's needs.
w: To explain to the patient what they need to know
Explaining is one part; the goal is meeting the patient's needs.
To determine the nature of the patient's problem
That's assessment, one part of it.
To improve the patient's physical health
It addresses emotional and informational needs too.
tf: The goal of therapeutic communication is to meet the patient's needs.
The goal of therapeutic communication is only to explain procedures.
It's about meeting the patient's needs.

items.q: Which of the following statements is true about a health care worker's communication with most older adults?
items.a: The communication needs of older adults can vary widely.
items.ex: Avoid stereotypes. Assess each older adult's needs rather than assuming hearing or memory problems.
w: The health care worker will have to talk slower when talking with older adults.
Not all older adults need slower speech; don't assume.
Older adults may not remember some of the information that is communicated.
The health care worker will have to talk louder when talking with older adults.
Many older adults hear well; don't assume.
tf: Older adults' communication needs vary widely.
You should always speak louder to older adults.
Don't assume; needs vary.

items.q: Which of the following would be best to help patients who are hospitalized and lonely or depressed?
items.ex: Listening shows patients you care and gives them a chance to express their feelings.
w: Have a hospital volunteer visit with them.
Visits can help, but you can listen yourself.
The focus should be on the patient.
Cheering up can dismiss their feelings.
items.hint: The simplest, most caring thing you can do.

items.q: Ana, a certified nursing assistant, enters the room of a postsurgical patient who is medicated, but obviously still experiencing a lot of pain. What should Ana say first?
items.ex: Always start by introducing yourself and your role, then identify the patient and address their needs.
w: Confirming identity matters, but introduce yourself first.
That's a social question; the patient is clearly in pain.
The pain is obvious; start by introducing yourself.

items.q: Which of the following illustrates a way to enhance a patient's self-esteem?
items.a: Involving the patient in decision-making whenever possible
items.ex: Involving patients in decisions shows you respect their judgment, which supports self-esteem.
w: Friendly, but involving them in decisions does more for self-esteem.
Explaining everything you are going to do in advance
Good practice, but less directly about self-esteem.
Shows attention, but decision-making builds self-esteem most.

items.q: Which of the following statements best describes the effect of nonverbal communication during oral communication exchanges?
items.a: It can express up to 70% of the sender's meaning.
items.ex: Body language, facial expressions, tone and gestures can carry up to 70% of a message's meaning.
w: Verbal and nonverbal communication usually express equal amounts of the meaning.
Nonverbal communication usually carries more of the meaning.
It reinforces the meaning of the verbal message.
It can also contradict the words.
It expresses a small part of the message's meaning.
tf: Nonverbal communication can express up to 70% of the sender's meaning.
Nonverbal communication expresses only a small part of a message's meaning.
It can carry up to 70%.
ty: Nonverbal communication can express up to ____% of a message's meaning.
Body language, facial expressions, tone and gestures can carry up to 70% of a message's meaning.

items.q: Why do some people with limited vision also have problems understanding oral communication?
items.a: They cannot see body language and facial expressions.
items.ex: Much of meaning is nonverbal; people who can't see it miss part of the message, so describe what you're doing and use tone carefully.
w: Vision problems sometimes also affect the ability to hear.
Vision and hearing are separate senses.
They don't know who is talking to them.
That can happen, but the main loss is nonverbal cues.
Limited vision affects the ability to concentrate.
items.hint: Think about the nonverbal part of a message.

items.q: Which statement is true about patients who are terminally ill?
items.a: Many patients who are terminally ill have a strong need to share their fears and concerns.
items.ex: Dying patients often want to talk about their fears. Listening and giving opportunities to express feelings helps.
w: Most patients who are facing death prefer to be left alone.
Many want company and someone to listen.
Patients who are terminally ill do not experience loneliness.
Patients near the end of life can no longer speak or hear.
Hearing often remains until the very end.
tf: Many terminally ill patients have a strong need to share their fears.
Most dying patients prefer to be left alone.
Many want to talk and be heard.

items.q: Which of the following is being demonstrated by a health care worker who is fully focused on what a patient is saying?
items.ex: Active listening means giving full attention, concentrating and observing, not just hearing words.
ty: Fully focusing on what someone is saying is called ________ listening.
active
Active listening means giving full attention, concentrating and observing, not just hearing words.

items.q: Which of the following actions is not necessarily a good way to help maintain the self-esteem of patients?
items.ex: Efficiency matters, but rushing can make patients feel unimportant. Respect, privacy and involvement support self-esteem.
w: Involve patients in decisions about their health.
items.hint: Which one is about you, not the patient?

items.q: Which of the following is the first step in the communication process?
items.ex: Steps of the communication process: set communication goals → create the message → deliver the message → listen to the response (and obtain feedback) → evaluate the communication throughout.
tf: The first step in the communication process is setting communication goals.
The first step in the communication process is delivering the message.
Goals come first.
items.hint: Know what you want to achieve.

items.q: Which of the following is a way to obtain feedback?
items.ex: Feedback techniques include reflecting, paraphrasing, asking questions and requesting examples.
w: Yes, but the others are also feedback techniques.
Yes, but the others are also feedback techniques.
Yes, but the others are also feedback techniques.

items.q: What is the best time for a health care worker to evaluate the communication related to an encounter with a patient?
items.ex: Evaluate continuously so you can adjust as you go. Steps of the communication process: set communication goals → create the message → deliver the message → listen to the response (and obtain feedback) → evaluate the communication throughout.
w: Evaluation shouldn't wait for one step.
At the end of the conversation
By then it may be too late to fix misunderstandings.
Feedback helps, but evaluation is continuous.

items.q: The percentage of Americans aged 75 and older who have significant hearing loss is ____
items.ex: About half of adults aged 75 and older have disabling hearing loss (NIDCD).
w: Too low for this age group.
Too low for this age group.
Close, but about half of adults 75+ have disabling hearing loss.
tf: About half of Americans 75 and older have significant hearing loss.
About 20% of Americans 75 and older have significant hearing loss.
It's about half.

items.q: Two health care workers are in the break room talking and laughing about the “weird clothes” worn by a coworker. This conversation is _____
items.a: An example of gossip that should not take place anywhere
items.ex: Gossip damages teamwork and trust. It's unprofessional anywhere.
w: Acceptable if the coworker cannot hear them
Gossip is unprofessional whether or not they hear.
Okay as long as they are on break
Okay if not done in the workplace
Gossip about coworkers is harmful anywhere.
items.hint: Is there any place it's okay?

items.q: When caring for patients who are terminally ill, health care professionals should
items.a: Give them opportunities to express their feelings
items.ex: Dying patients often need to talk about fears and feelings; give them chances to do so.
w: Make an effort not to disturb them
Use humor to cheer them up
Humor can seem dismissive if it isn't welcome.

items.q: The use of feedback in communication is intended to ____
items.a: Help both senders and receivers increase their understanding of each other
items.ex: Feedback lets both sides check understanding: the sender learns if the message was received as intended, and the receiver confirms what they heard.
w: Increase the interaction between senders and receivers
More interaction isn't the goal; understanding is.
Help listeners know if they have understood the sender’s message
It helps both sides, not only the listener.
Help senders know if their message was interpreted correctly
It helps both sides, not only the sender.
items.hint: Who benefits: one side or both?

items.q: Touching a patient's shoulder or hand can be an effective way of communicating.
items.ex: Appropriate touch can show care and comfort, as long as it suits the patient and their culture.
items.ww: Touch can communicate care when appropriate.

items.q: If a patient states they are “fine,” but their body language indicates that they are worried, it is likely that _____
items.ex: When verbal and nonverbal messages conflict, the nonverbal message is usually the true one.
w: When words and body language conflict, body language is usually more accurate.
The message is mixed, but the nonverbal part shows the real feeling.
tf: When words and body language conflict, body language usually shows the true feeling.
When words and body language conflict, the words usually show the true feeling.
Body language is usually more accurate.

items.q: When speaking to an older woman who is a new patient, the medical assistant should ______
items.a: Ask the patient how  she wishes to be addressed
items.ex: Ask patients how they'd like to be addressed. Until then, use a title and last name.
w: Call the patient by her first name
First names may seem disrespectful to some older adults.

items.q: Which of the following actions is appropriate when communicating with an individual who has hearing loss?
items.a: Direct a light source on your face
items.ex: Good lighting on your face helps the person read lips and expressions. Face them, speak clearly and pause.
w: Face the person so they can see your lips and expressions.
Shouting distorts speech; speak clearly at a normal or slightly louder level.
tf: Lighting your face helps a person with hearing loss read your lips.
Sitting next to a person with hearing loss helps them understand you.
Face them instead so they can see your lips.
items.hint: They need to see your lips.

items.q: The physical environment can influence the effectiveness of communication.
items.ex: Noise, lighting, privacy and comfort all affect communication.
items.ww: Noise, privacy and lighting all matter.

items.q: With which of the following patients might pantomime be an effective method of communication?
items.a: A patient who understands very little English
items.ex: Gestures and acting things out can bridge a language barrier (along with an interpreter).
w: A patient who is almost completely blind
A patient who is in pain
A patient who is very upset

items.q: If a patient with Alzheimer’s disease states that it is Sunday when it is Tuesday, the best response would be to respond by saying, ______
items.ex: Correct gently without arguing or testing the patient's memory.
w: Flatly contradicting can upset the patient.
"Don't you remember?" is distressing for people with memory loss.
“Why do you think today is Sunday?”
Asking them to reason it out can frustrate them.

items.q: To control your nerves when speaking to a group, it is best not to look at the audience.
items.ex: Eye contact helps you connect and stay engaged; practice and preparation help with nerves.
items.ww: Look at the audience to connect.

items.q: Using lots of casual words and fillers, such as "you know," is a good way to put patients at ease.
items.ex: Fillers make you sound unprofessional and unclear. Speak clearly and warmly.

items.q: When working with adults who have aphasia, use simple, child-like language.
items.ex: Use simple, clear language, but speak to them as adults; aphasia affects language, not intelligence.
items.ww: Use simple language, but never talk down to adults.

items.q: Which of the following is an example of a good learning objective?
items.a: The patient will be able to correctly change the dressing on their incision.
items.ex: Good learning objectives describe a specific, measurable action the learner will be able to do.
w: The nurse will explain the details of wound care.
Objectives describe what the learner will do, not the teacher.
The patient will learn about wound care.
The class will discuss wound care.
tf: A good learning objective describes something measurable the learner will be able to do.
"The patient will learn about wound care" is a good learning objective.
That can't be measured.
items.hint: Can you observe and measure it?

items.q: Which of the following questions is most likely to help a nurse learn about the needs of a patient?
items.ex: A focused, open question about how the patient feels right now invites them to describe their needs.
w: That's a social greeting that often gets "fine."
"What is your pain level on a scale of 0 to 10?"
Useful, but it only covers pain.
items.hint: Open, focused on the patient right now.

items.q: Today's patients need more education and information from health care professionals than they did in the past.
items.ex: Shorter hospital stays and more self-care at home mean patients need more education.

items.q: Effective listening can be hindered by receivers' reactions to what the sender is saying.
items.ex: Emotional reactions, judgments and planning your reply can block listening.
items.ww: Reactions can get in the way of listening.

items.q: Listening and understanding take place at a faster rate than the rate of speech.
items.ex: We can think much faster than people speak, which is why the mind can wander while listening.
items.ww: The mind works faster than speech.

items.q: A patient has just learned they have cancer and is feeling depressed. The best thing to do is to _______.
items.a: invite them to talk about their feelings
items.ex: Inviting patients to share their feelings is therapeutic; false reassurance and cheering up are not.
w: tell them to have positive thoughts
assure them you know how they feel
No one can truly know how another feels.

items.q: Many Americans only read at a grade school level and do not understand instructions on prescription bottles.
items.ex: Low health literacy is common, so use plain language and check understanding.

items.q: The health care professional can enhance a patient's self-esteem by communicating courteously and respectfully.
items.ex: Courtesy and respect show patients they are valued.

items.q: Which of the following is the best example of successful communication by a pharmacy technician instructing a customer about how to take a new medication?
items.a: The pharmacy technician used feedback and determined that they understood the instructions.
items.ex: Success is confirmed by feedback, such as having the customer explain the instructions back (teach-back).
w: The pharmacy technician told them to read the instructions included with the medication.
The pharmacy technician asked them if they understood the instructions and they said "Yes."
People often say yes without understanding; ask them to explain it back.
The pharmacy technician gave them the medication and thanked them for their business.
items.hint: How do you KNOW they understood?

items.q: Which of the following is true about nonverbal communication?
items.a: It can express up to 70% of the sender's message.
items.ex: Nonverbal communication carries much of a message's meaning and is often unconscious.
w: It is not important if the spoken message is clear.
Nonverbal cues can contradict even clear words.
Most people do not pay much attention to nonverbal communication.
ty: Nonverbal communication can express up to ____% of a message.
Nonverbal communication carries much of a message's meaning and is often unconscious.

items.q: "I think what I hear you saying is that you don't feel any better after taking the medication," is an example of which feedback technique?
items.ex: Paraphrasing restates the speaker's message in your own words to check understanding.
w: That isn't a feedback technique here.
Reflecting mirrors the speaker's words back; this restates the meaning in new words.
tf: Restating a patient's message in your own words is paraphrasing.
Restating a patient's message in your own words is requesting an example.
That's paraphrasing.
ty: Restating someone's message in your own words is called ________.
paraphrasing
paraphrase
Paraphrasing restates the speaker's message in your own words to check understanding.

mt.q: Match each feedback technique to what it does.
pairs: Restating the message in your own words
mt.ex: Paraphrasing restates the speaker's message in your own words to check understanding.

items.hint: Saying it in your own words.

items.q: The use of touch is a common nonverbal form of communication that can be used with all patients to communicate care and interest.
items.ex: Touch isn't welcome for everyone; culture, trauma history and personal preference matter.

items.q: Which of the following is a recommendation for good telephone communication?
items.a: Smile as you speak unless it is inappropriate
items.ex: Smiling changes your tone of voice and makes you sound friendly on the phone.
w: Speak clearly at a moderate, not slow, pace.
items.hint: People can hear it in your voice.

items.q: It is important that health care professionals control their facial expressions when working with patients.
items.ex: Expressions of shock or disgust can upset patients; keep a calm, caring expression.

items.q: Speaking a little louder than normal can help non-English speakers understand what you are saying.
items.ex: Volume doesn't help with a language barrier. Use simple words, gestures and an interpreter.
items.ww: Louder doesn't fix a language barrier.

items.q: Which of the following is not a helpful technique for communicating with someone who has dementia?
items.ex: With dementia: use simple words, repeat the same words rather than rephrasing, and don't argue or reason. Long, unfilled pauses can lose the person's attention, so this is the choice the course marks as not helpful (giving a little time to respond is still good).
w: Do not try to reason with the patient
Reasoning and arguing frustrate people with dementia, so this is helpful advice.
Repeat rather than rephrase if the patient does not understand what is being said
Repeating the same words is less confusing, so this is helpful.
items.hint: Which one could cause the person to lose track?

items.q: What type of question is, "What is your date of birth?"?
items.ex: Closed-ended questions have a short, specific answer, like a date or yes/no.
w: Probing questions dig deeper into something already said.
ty: "What is your date of birth?" is a ________-ended question.
closed
close
Closed-ended questions have a short, specific answer, like a date or yes/no.

mt.q: Match each type of question to an example.
pairs: "Can you tell me more about that?"
mt.ex: Closed-ended questions have a short, specific answer, like a date or yes/no.

items.q: Humor is usually not appropriate for patients who are ill or injured.
items.ex: Gentle, appropriate humor can relieve tension; read the situation and the patient.

items.q: Many patients do not understand the information they are given by their health care providers but are too embarrassed to admit it.
items.ex: That's why you check understanding with feedback, like teach-back, instead of asking "Do you understand?"

items.q: Communication among health care professionals is as important as communication with patients.
items.ex: Clear team communication prevents errors and keeps care coordinated.
items.ww: Team communication is critical to safety.

items.q: Which of the following is a type of probing question?
items.a: “Can you tell me more about when you get these headaches?"
items.ex: Probing questions follow up to get more detail about something the patient has already mentioned.
w: "Would you describe the pain as dull, throbbing, or aching?"
That's open-ended, but it doesn't follow up on something already said.
ty: A follow-up question that asks for more detail is a ________ question.
probing
Probing questions follow up to get more detail about something the patient has already mentioned.

items.q: Which website address extension below is used by entities such as the National Institutes of Health and the Food and Drug Administration?
items.ex: U.S. government agencies use .gov, which is generally a reliable source of health information.
w: .org is used by organizations, often nonprofits.
tf: Government agencies like the NIH and FDA use .gov web addresses.
Government agencies like the NIH and FDA use .com web addresses.
.com is commercial; government sites use .gov.
ty: Government agency websites end in ____.
.gov
gov
U.S. government agencies use .gov, which is generally a reliable source of health information.

items.q: Which law specifically addresses the privacy of medical records?
items.a: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)
items.ex: HIPAA sets national rules protecting the privacy and security of patients' health information.
w: FAERS is a database of drug safety reports, not a law.
A.D.A.M. is a medical information resource, not a law.
tf: HIPAA protects the privacy of medical records.
FAERS is the law that protects the privacy of medical records.
FAERS is a drug-safety database; HIPAA is the privacy law.
ty: The law protecting the privacy of health information is ________. (abbreviation)
HIPAA
HIPAA sets national rules protecting the privacy and security of patients' health information.

items.q: Which of the following statements best describes the meaning of being a computer-literate health care professional?
items.a: Having the knowledge and skills to perform the computer tasks required for one's job
items.ex: Computer literacy means being able to efficiently do the computer tasks required for your own job.
w: Knowing how to use many software programs
It's about the tasks your job needs, not as many programs as possible.
Understanding how computers work and how to troubleshoot problems
Being able to conduct extensive research using the computer
Research is one possible task, not the definition.
tf: Computer literacy means having the skills to perform the computer tasks your job requires.
Computer literacy means being able to repair computers.
It means doing your job's computer tasks.

items.q: Which of the following is not a guideline for writing professional emails?
items.a: Using all caps or all lowercase for the body of the email
items.ex: All caps reads as shouting, and all lowercase looks careless. Use normal capitalization, proofread, keep a professional tone and leave out confidential information.
tf: Writing an email in all capital letters is like shouting.
Writing professional emails in all lowercase is recommended.
Use normal capitalization.

items.q: Which of the answers below describes what the Electronic Communication Privacy Act of 1986 provides?
items.a: Protection against unauthorized access or interception of data communications
items.ex: The Electronic Communications Privacy Act protects electronic communications, such as email, from being intercepted or accessed without authorization.
w: That's covered by copyright and academic rules.
Regulations of site licenses and networking
Guidelines for communications between health care providers and patients
That's not what this act covers.

items.q: Which technology allows patients to be monitored by health care professionals in their own homes?
items.ex: Telemedicine is the use of medical information exchanged from one site to another through electronic communication to improve a patient's health, such as remote monitoring, video visits and consultations.
w: Fiber optics carries light through thin cables, for example in endoscopes.
That's an online group of people.
ty: Monitoring patients at home through electronic communication is called ________.
telemedicine
telehealth

Telemedicine is the use of medical information exchanged from one site to another through electronic communication to improve a patient's health, such as remote monitoring, video visits and consultations.

items.q: Which of the following technologies allows surgeons to see inside the body without making a large incision?
items.ex: Fiber-optic scopes carry light and images through thin flexible fibers, allowing minimally invasive procedures through small openings.
w: That's using computers to manage biological data.
X-rays create images but don't let a surgeon see inside during surgery.
tf: Fiber optics lets surgeons see inside the body through small incisions.
Bioinformatics lets surgeons see inside the body through small incisions.
That's fiber optics.
ty: Thin cables that carry light let surgeons see inside the body. This is fiber ________.
optics
Fiber-optic scopes carry light and images through thin flexible fibers, allowing minimally invasive procedures through small openings.

items.q: Which of the statements below illustrates a major obstacle to the use of telemedicine?
items.a: Some state licensing laws prohibit physicians from practicing medicine across state lines.
items.ex: Physicians are licensed by state, so treating patients in other states can be legally restricted. Rural internet access is another obstacle.
w: Many patients use and value telemedicine.
The lack of adequate technology doesn't allow the transmission of images and information.
Most physicians resist working with distant patients.

items.q: Which of the following statements is not true about robotic surgery?
items.a: Robots are rapidly replacing the need for human surgeons.
items.ex: In robotic surgery a human surgeon controls the robot. Robots assist surgeons; they don't replace them.
w: It is now used for many types of surgery.
There is a decreased risk of infection.
True: smaller incisions lower infection risk.
The incisions are much smaller than in traditional surgeries.
tf: In robotic surgery, a human surgeon controls the robot.
Robots are rapidly replacing human surgeons.
Surgeons control the robots.

items.q: Which of the following statements describes the purpose of the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database?
items.a: Track and help prevent medication errors.
items.ex: FAERS collects reports of adverse drug events and medication errors so the FDA can spot safety problems.
ty: The FDA's database of drug side effects and medication errors is called ________. (abbreviation)
FAERS
FAERS collects reports of adverse drug events and medication errors so the FDA can spot safety problems.

items.q: Which of the following is an example of a database?
items.a: Records of all clinic's patients organized by name, address, and insurance company
items.ex: A database is a collection of data organized in a structured way so it can be searched and sorted.
w: Billing software uses data but is a program, not the organized collection itself.
The patient instruction sheets that a clinic has stored on the computer
Those are documents, not organized data.
A list of useful Internet sites for employee use
A simple list isn't a structured database.
tf: A database is a collection of data organized in a structured way.
Patient instruction sheets saved on a computer are a database.
Documents aren't a structured database.
ty: A collection of data organized in a structured way is a ________.
database
A database is a collection of data organized in a structured way so it can be searched and sorted.

items.q: Which type of information should never be included in or attached to an email?
items.ex: Regular email isn't secure; patient records shouldn't be sent this way.

items.q: Which of the answers below is the definition of a network?
items.a: Computers and other devices linked together to exchange information
items.ex: A network links computers and devices so they can share information and resources.
w: A backup service that runs on the Internet
Permission to install software on more than one computer
ty: Computers linked together to share information form a ________.
network
A network links computers and devices so they can share information and resources.

items.q: Which of the following is likely to be the least reliable source of information about type 2 diabetes?
items.a: A commercial website selling natural products that it claims are safer to take than prescribed medications for treating type 2 diabetes.
items.ex: Sites selling products have a financial motive and often make unsupported claims.
w: A research paper published by a university press that studied the effects of lifestyle habits on the incidence of diabetes.
Reports from the National Institutes of Health.
Patient information presented on the American Diabetes Association website.

items.q: Which type of software could a clinic use to estimate the number of doses of flu vaccine it will need next year?
items.ex: Spreadsheets do numerical calculations and projections, like budgets and supply estimates.
w: Databases store and sort records; spreadsheets do calculations and projections.
ty: Software for calculations and projections is an electronic ________.
spreadsheet
Spreadsheets do numerical calculations and projections, like budgets and supply estimates.

mt.q: Match each technology to what it's used for.
mt.ex: Spreadsheets do numerical calculations and projections, like budgets and supply estimates.

items.q: Which of the following is used to back up data?
items.ex: Back up data to external hard drives or cloud storage so it isn't lost.
w: RAM is temporary memory that clears when the computer is off.
Lasers are used in surgery and treatment.

items.q: What is the goal of computer literacy for health care professionals?
items.ex: Computer literacy lets professionals do their job's computer tasks efficiently.
w: Setting up databases of patient information
items.hint: Doing your job's computer work well.

items.q: Which of the terms below refers to the use of medical information exchanged from one site to another via electronic communications to improve a patient's clinical health status?
items.ex: Telemedicine is the use of medical information exchanged from one site to another through electronic communication to improve a patient's health, such as remote monitoring, video visits and consultations.
w: Networks are the linked computers, not the medical practice.
ty: Using electronically exchanged medical information to improve a patient's health is ________.
telemedicine
telehealth

Telemedicine is the use of medical information exchanged from one site to another through electronic communication to improve a patient's health, such as remote monitoring, video visits and consultations.

items.q: Which requirement for the use of technology is an obstacle for facilities in rural areas?
items.a: Adequate infrastructure to support high-speed wireless
items.ex: Many rural areas lack the high-speed internet infrastructure that telemedicine needs.

sc.title: Jodi, MRI technologist
sc.text:
Jodi is an MRI technologist at a busy hospital, conducting diagnostic imaging procedures for patients. With advancements in technology, Jodi’s job has evolved to incorporate various computer-based tools and techniques to enhance the quality and efficiency of imaging services.

One day, Jodi encounters a patient who requires an MRI scan to assess a suspected spinal injury. Using specialized imaging software and equipment, Jodi performs the scan with precision, capturing detailed images of the patient's spine. Throughout the process, Jodi ensures the accuracy of the images and maintains patient comfort and safety.

history

sc.text:
Nathan works as a medical coder in the billing department of a large hospital. The role involves reviewing patient medical records and assigning appropriate codes for billing purposes. Nathan ensures accuracy and compliance with coding guidelines to facilitate timely and accurate reimbursement for medical services provided.

Nathan encounters a complex case involving a patient who underwent multiple procedures during a single hospitalization. Nathan carefully reviews the patient's medical records, which include provider notes, laboratory results, and diagnostic imaging reports. Nathan meticulously assigns the appropriate procedure codes based on the documented information, considering the patient's diagnosis and treatment plan.

items.q: Which statement is true about the Veterans Health Administration (VA)?
items.a: It is the largest integrated health system in the United States.

sc.title: Iman, medical assistant
sc.text: Iman works as a medical assistant in a primary care clinic. Responsibilities include assisting providers with office visits, collecting patient medical histories, and coordinating patient appointments. Iman notices discrepancies in the clinic's billing records and patient insurance claims after one of the clinic patients, Susan, comes in with a bill that came in the mail. Susan states that the bill reflects an office visit that was billed to Medicare, Susan’s primary insurance plan, but was not billed to Susan’s second private insurance plan. Iman finds that the clinic does not have the second private insurance plan on file for Susan. sc.title: Josie, pharmacy technician
sc.text: Josie works as a pharmacy technician in a busy hospital pharmacy. The role involves preparing and dispensing medications for patients, as well as ensuring accuracy and safety in medication administration. Josie notices a discrepancy in medication orders for a patient scheduled for surgery. Josie believes that the prescription dose was written for twice the amount of medication that is safe. Josie is concerned about the potential for a medication error and the patient’s safety. Josie contacts the prescribing provider and receives the correct medication dose for the prescription. Josie also finds out that there is an issue with the communication system that sends the prescriptions from the electronic health record (EHR) to the pharmacy. Josie wants to take proactive measures to address the issue in a timely manner and improve the communication system to ensure prescriptions are transmitted correctly.
